questions.text: What is the difference between shell and terminal?

answers.feedback: The shell (bash, zsh) is the command interpreter. The terminal (GNOME Terminal, Windows Terminal) is the terminal emulator — the graphical interface.

questions.text: In a fresh shell, VAR has not been exported. After VAR='test', what does bash -c 'echo $VAR' display?

answers.feedback: A newly invoked bash -c receives exported variables. A parenthesised subshell (echo $VAR) inherits shell variables even without export; these are different cases.

questions.text: What does exit code 0 signify in Linux?

answers.feedback: Exit status 0 conventionally means success. Nonzero indicates failure or another command-specific outcome, such as grep finding no matches. Inspect $? immediately.

questions.text: Expansion-only question: with DIR=/home/user versus DIR empty, what pathname does "$DIR/temp" denote? Do not execute the illustrative rm commands.

answers.feedback: An empty DIR makes both $DIR/temp and "$DIR/temp" refer to /temp. Quoting prevents splitting and globbing, but validate a non-empty intended directory before deletion. A deletion command would target that path; whether removal succeeds depends on existence, permissions and the tool.
